item.content:encoded:
Naval Air Station Pensacola will close its gates to the public on Wednesday, November 5, according to a media advisory from the base. The closure is being implemented to accommodate a STEAM Day event — an educational program focused on science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics.

The base did not specify what time the closure would begin or end, or provide details about which areas of the installation would be affected. Visitors planning to tour NAS Pensacola or access the flight line or museum should plan their visits for other days this week.

For more information about NAS Pensacola's visiting hours or upcoming events, contact the base public affairs office.

item.title: Pensacola Beach Chamber Celebrates Successful 18th Annual Taste of the Beach
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Pensacola Beach Chamber of Commerce wrapped up its 18th Annual Taste of the Beach over the weekend, calling the event a major success for the island community. The multi-day festival featured a sunset cruise with dolphin sightings, a VIP trolley dinner, a Saturday festival, and a Sunday brunch experience. The chamber highlighted the…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Beach Chamber of Commerce wrapped up its 18th Annual Taste of the Beach over the weekend, calling the event a major success for the island community. The multi-day festival featured a sunset cruise with dolphin sightings, a VIP trolley dinner, a Saturday festival, and a Sunday brunch experience.

The chamber highlighted the participation of dozens of local restaurants and businesses, including Baja Coastal Kitchen, Flounder's Chowder House, Salt, Shaggy's, and Crabs on the Beach. Innisfree Hotels served as the event's premier sponsor. According to the chamber, the weekend drew significant attendance and provided a boost to local dining and hospitality businesses.

"From a magical Sunset Cruise filled with dolphins, music, and breathtaking views, to our fabulous VIP Trolley Dinner, a fun-filled Saturday Festival, and a delicious Sunday Brunch Trolley, it was a weekend celebrating everything we love about Pensacola Beach," the chamber said in a statement.

With Taste of the Beach now behind them, the Pensacola Beach Chamber is shifting focus to the holiday season, announcing plans for "Season Your Holidays on Pensacola Beach" events in the coming weeks.

item.title: USDA Awards $10M for Florida Land Conservation in Lake Wales Ridge
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Natural Resources Conservation Service announced Tuesday it is awarding $10 million to protect agricultural and natural lands in Central Florida's Lake Wales Ridge ecosystem. The five-year Lake Wales Ridge Ecosystem Regional Conservation Partnership Program project, led by Tampa-based nonprofit Wildlands…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Natural Resources Conservation Service announced Tuesday it is awarding $10 million to protect agricultural and natural lands in Central Florida's Lake Wales Ridge ecosystem. The five-year Lake Wales Ridge Ecosystem Regional Conservation Partnership Program project, led by Tampa-based nonprofit Wildlands Conservation, will focus on Marion, Lake, Polk, and Highlands counties when it begins in 2027, according to the USDA-NRCS.

The initiative aims to expand conservation easements—voluntary legal agreements that permanently limit development while keeping land in private ownership—allowing farmers and ranchers to continue compatible operations while protecting environmental values. The program targets a region where citrus greening disease and rapid development pressure threaten both the agricultural economy and critical wildlife habitat. Partners include Polk Forever, the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Archbold Research Station, and Putnam Land Conservancy.

"By expanding conservation easement opportunities in the Lake Wales Ridge area, we can help keep working lands in agriculture in one of the fastest developing regions of Florida," said Juan Hernandez, NRCS State Conservationist for Florida. The project will help protect rural lands that support the Florida Wildlife Corridor and complement military training needs at nearby Avon Park Air Force Range. The $10 million federal award will be matched by similar funding from county and state land protection programs.

Landowners interested in learning more can contact Wildlands Conservation at 813-252-6517 or info@wildlandsconservation.org.

item.title: I-10 Westbound Closed at MM 19 After Dump Truck Rollover
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The closure began around 12:30 p.m. Tuesday. Traffic is being diverted around the accident through the emergency lane, but drivers should…
item.content:encoded:
The westbound lanes of Interstate 10 are shut down at mile marker 19 in Santa Rosa County following a rolled dump truck that has spilled asphalt across the roadway, according to Santa Rosa County Communications.

The closure began around 12:30 p.m. Tuesday. Traffic is being diverted around the accident through the emergency lane, but drivers should expect major delays in the area. Emergency responders and utility crews are working the scene, and the duration of the closure remains unclear at this time.

The county is urging motorists to use extra caution, allow additional travel time, and stay alert for emergency personnel. For real-time traffic updates, drivers can check the Florida Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles incident map at trafficincidents.flhsmv.gov or call FL511.

item.content:encoded:
An Escambia County Sheriff's Office deputy has been placed on paid administrative leave following a shooting incident that occurred just after midnight early Tuesday morning, according to an ECSO news release reported by WKRG News 5.

The incident unfolded when another man pulled out a handgun, prompting the deputy to fire a weapon. Details about the circumstances leading up to the confrontation, the location of the incident, and whether anyone was injured remain unclear from the initial report.

The use of force is now under review as standard protocol calls for administrative leave in such cases. The Escambia County Sheriff's Office has not yet released additional details about the investigation or timeline for further updates.

item.title: NAS Pensacola Hosts Blue Angels Media Day, STEAM Event Nov. 5

The day will feature a Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Math (STEAM) Day for eligible participants, along with a media availability session with select Blue Angels…
item.content:encoded:
Naval Air Station Pensacola is gearing up for its 2026 Homecoming Airshow with two events scheduled for Wednesday, November 5, according to a media advisory from the base.

The day will feature a Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Math (STEAM) Day for eligible participants, along with a media availability session with select Blue Angels service members. The Blue Angels will serve as the headlining act for the upcoming airshow.

Access to NAS Pensacola on November 5 is restricted to Department of Defense identification card holders only. Additional restrictions apply to the flightline, which will be accessible only to DoD ID card holders in uniform. The base emphasized that these are not public events.

Further details about the 2026 NAS Pensacola Homecoming Airshow are expected as the event date approaches.

item.title: Santa Rosa County to host Veterans Day ceremonies, offices closed Nov. 11
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County will observe Veterans Day on Wednesday, November 11, with multiple ceremonies honoring military service members and several county office closures. The Veterans Memorial Plaza in Milton will host a Veterans Day ceremony and wreath-laying at 11 a.m. at 5191 Willing Street. Following the ceremony, attendees are invited to American…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County will observe Veterans Day on Wednesday, November 11, with multiple ceremonies honoring military service members and several county office closures.

The Veterans Memorial Plaza in Milton will host a Veterans Day ceremony and wreath-laying at 11 a.m. at 5191 Willing Street. Following the ceremony, attendees are invited to American Legion Post #78 at 6025 Spikes Way for a flag retirement ceremony, bonfire, and cookout. The meal will be provided by Grover's Restaurant and served by Santa Rosa County 4-H Club members and volunteers. For details, contact Veterans Memorial at 850-860-2427 or email santarosa.veterans.memorial.plaza@gmail.com.

VFW Post 4407 in Gulf Breeze will also hold a ceremony at 11 a.m. at 1783 Abercrombie Road, presented by Veterans of Foreign Wars Post 4407.

Most Santa Rosa County offices will be closed Wednesday, including the Board of Commissioners, library system, veterans services, animal services, and extension services. However, the central landfill will remain open, and essential services including 9-1-1 dispatch, Lifeguard Ambulance Service, and fire departments will operate normally. The Clerk of Court, Property Appraiser, Supervisor of Elections, and Tax Collector will also be closed.

item.title: Polls Open Today in Escambia, Santa Rosa Counties; Voting Until 7 p.m.
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida's polls are open today from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time for Election Day voting. Voters in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties — along with seven other Northwest Florida counties and part of Gulf County — are on Central Time, meaning they're one hour behind the rest of the state. That means the polls in our area close at 7 p.m. Central Time,…
item.content:encoded:
Florida's polls are open today from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time for Election Day voting.

Voters in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties — along with seven other Northwest Florida counties and part of Gulf County — are on Central Time, meaning they're one hour behind the rest of the state. That means the polls in our area close at 7 p.m. Central Time, or 8 p.m. Eastern Time.

If you're heading to the polls, make sure you know your polling location and bring a valid photo ID. For voters who haven't cast a ballot yet, today is the final day to vote in person.

item.content:encoded:
Buoy readings off Pensacola are showing elevated ocean conditions Tuesday, with significant wave heights reaching 6.2 feet, according to Florida Gulf Signal. Easterly winds are running at 17.5 knots, with wave periods of 7 seconds. Air temperature was holding at 77.5°F at the time of the report.

The moderate seas are typical of fall conditions in the Gulf of Mexico and pose manageable conditions for most recreational and commercial marine traffic, though boaters should remain aware of the elevated swells.

item.title: Escambia County voting surges ahead of Election Day
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Early voting in Escambia County is tracking at about 32 percent as of Monday, with thousands of Florida voters already casting ballots before polls open statewide Tuesday for the midterm elections. Across Florida, nearly 40 percent of registered voters have already participated in early voting or requested mail-in ballots ahead of Election Day,…
item.content:encoded:
Early voting in Escambia County is tracking at about 32 percent as of Monday, with thousands of Florida voters already casting ballots before polls open statewide Tuesday for the midterm elections.

Across Florida, nearly 40 percent of registered voters have already participated in early voting or requested mail-in ballots ahead of Election Day, according to reports from North Escambia. The strong early turnout suggests robust participation in this year's midterm contests.

Escambia County voters can cast ballots at their regular polling locations Tuesday, or those who haven't already voted early can visit their designated precinct on Election Day. Poll locations open at 7 a.m. and close at 7 p.m.

item.content:encoded:

The community is invited to welcome the new team during a public ceremony at the stadium on Monday, November 16, at 5:00 p.m. The event will mark an official introduction of the franchise to the Pensacola area.

The addition of the Florida Vibe expands professional sports offerings in the region and adds another tenant to Blue Wahoos Stadium, which currently hosts the Pensacola Blue Wahoos minor league baseball team.

item.content:encoded:
Area high schools are wrapping up their regular season with makeup games this week after Hurricane Isaias forced postponements earlier in the fall.

Tuesday night's matchups include Navarre at Tate, Gulf Breeze at Escambia, Washington at Milton, Pine Forest at Pensacola, and South Walton at West Florida.

Wednesday's slate features Northview at Blountstown, Pace at Niceville, and Jay at Marianna. These games represent the final regular-season action for most area programs before the postseason gets underway.

item.title: Warm Tuesday Before Rain and Cool-Down Wednesday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola-area residents can expect pleasant conditions today with highs climbing near 80 degrees, but a weather system moving through will bring increasing shower chances this afternoon and widespread rain overnight into Wednesday, according to the National Weather Service. The most significant rain activity is expected Tuesday night through…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola-area residents can expect pleasant conditions today with highs climbing near 80 degrees, but a weather system moving through will bring increasing shower chances this afternoon and widespread rain overnight into Wednesday, according to the National Weather Service.

The most significant rain activity is expected Tuesday night through Wednesday morning as the system pushes through Northwest Florida. Thunderstorms are likely during that window, so residents should be prepared for wet conditions if heading to the polls today.

Once the system clears, skies will improve and a noticeable cooling trend takes hold as we head toward the weekend, bringing more seasonal fall temperatures back to the area.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County voters head to the polls today, Tuesday, November 3, for Election Day. Polling places across the county are open and accepting ballots for local, state, and federal races.

According to NorthEscambia.com, election results will begin posting to their Facebook page shortly after polls close this evening. Complete local and state results are expected to be available on their website and social media channels Wednesday morning.

If you haven't voted yet, check your voter registration status and polling location at your county supervisor of elections office or online voter portal.

item.title: Cantonment Man Faces Felony Charges in Nearly 200 Fraudulent Fuel Card Scheme
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The alleged scheme involved repeated fraudulent transactions, with the suspect accused of misusing the…
item.content:encoded:
A Cantonment resident is facing felony charges after investigators say he used a company fuel card to make nearly 200 unauthorized gas purchases for his personal vehicle over approximately 20 months, according to reporting from North Escambia.

The alleged scheme involved repeated fraudulent transactions, with the suspect accused of misusing the card entrusted to him for legitimate business purposes. The investigation focused on the pattern of unauthorized activity spanning the extended period.

Details on the specific employer, exact dollar amount of losses, or the timeline of the investigation were not immediately available. The case has been referred for prosecution.

item.title: Gulf Shores moves to restore local control of Fat Tuesday parade
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: After months of negotiation, Gulf Shores city leaders are working toward an agreement that would return the city's Fat Tuesday parade to local krewes, according to WKRG News 5. The move comes as the Alabama coastal city seeks to reinvigorate its Mardi Gras tradition through a new partnership structure that gives community organizations greater…
item.content:encoded: After months of negotiation, Gulf Shores city leaders are working toward an agreement that would return the city's Fat Tuesday parade to local krewes, according to WKRG News 5. The move comes as the Alabama coastal city seeks to reinvigorate its Mardi Gras tradition through a new partnership structure that gives community organizations greater oversight of the longtime celebration. Details of the agreement remain in development, but the shift represents an effort to preserve the parade while distributing responsibility among local groups rather than maintaining centralized city management.

item.content:encoded:
The Shrimp Basket, a seafood restaurant chain that originated in Gulf Shores, has shuttered six locations, according to reporting from WPMI NBC 15. The closures include the Bay Minette restaurant, marking a significant contraction for the regional chain.

The company has not yet released a public statement detailing the reasons for the closures or the timeline for when the locations ceased operations. It remains unclear how many Shrimp Basket restaurants remain open or whether additional closures are planned.
